subject: [hw] opus-perf: vpud GET_LOG_OBJECT busy loop burns a full core and floods the log (top CPU risk for the daemon)
body: Measured with the guest instruction counter on opus-venc /tmp tree (reaches M-f, 6 frames): a vpud thread (code in vpud itself, not the codec libs) polls GET_LOG_OBJECT on /dev/vcu, and because the V40 model answers immediately it never sleeps: each turn = ioctl + malloc + strnlen + strstr x14 + free + __android_log_print("[Invalid debug cmd] size: 1. set param ...") . Over one session: 1.9 G guest instructions, 4.57 M ioctls, 4.57 M log lines (136 MB runner log at 1080p). The codec work itself is tiny (11-13 k guest instructions per frame). On the phone this thread would hold one core at 100% and flood the console. Request (V40): make GET_LOG_OBJECT behave like the kernel for an idle log, i.e. block (bounded, e.g. wait up to 1 s / until stop) or return the answer vpud treats as "nothing to do" so it sleeps; IV PROGRESS already noted the 805506 calls/5 s. Evidence: gpu/hwcodec/tests/perf/run_vmix.sh --tree /tmp/n2hw-venc/src/gpu/hwcodec, phase "close"/"start" top function = vpud:?, host calls strstr 64 M / ioctl 4.6 M.
